basement.first: B3, stencilled on the blockwork beside the opening. The work order in your pocket says the same thing.

keyPuzzle.first: A rekey ledger: REPLACEMENT LOCK — CHAPEL — CABINET C-17.
Tag: CH-04. CHAPEL — MAIN, stamped into the brass. The stamp is older than the ring.
keyPuzzle.again: CH-04. The chapel door this was cut for is still there. The lock in it is not.

keyPuzzle.first: Tag: C-17. A cabinet number in biro, written over a scratched-out one.
keyPuzzle.again: C-17. Newer than the ring it is on, and nobody has stamped it yet.

keyPuzzle.first: Tag: FOH-M. FRONT OF HOUSE — MASTER. Worn smooth on both faces.
keyPuzzle.again: FOH-M. It opens everything on this side of the doors and nothing past them.

civicExterior.first: DEMOLITION NOTICE. Works commence 06:00 Thursday. The contractor is a name you have never heard of and the client is W. ELLERY HOLDINGS, which is the name on your work order.
civicExterior.again: Six on Thursday. The board beside it still counts down in fourteens, and stopped being changed some time in March.

civicExterior.first: ELLERY MUNICIPAL SCHOOL OF MUSIC · OPENED 1888. The older name is cut deeper than the current one.
civicExterior.again: ELLERY MUNICIPAL SCHOOL OF MUSIC · OPENED 1888. The older name is cut deeper than the current one.

civicExterior.first: ELLERY COLLEGIATE CHAPEL · 1908. The tower came after the school and has spent a century pretending otherwise.
civicExterior.again: ELLERY COLLEGIATE CHAPEL · 1908. The tower came after the school and has spent a century pretending otherwise.

civicExterior.first: MUNICIPAL BATHS · 1912. Blue tesserae survive under the paint. The pool was public before it belonged to the conservatoire.
civicExterior.again: MUNICIPAL BATHS · 1912. Blue tesserae survive under the paint. The pool was public before it belonged to the conservatoire.

civicExterior.first: CONCERT HALL · 1936. The fly tower is eight metres behind this low range, where a stage tower belongs.
civicExterior.again: CONCERT HALL · 1936. The fly tower is eight metres behind this low range, where a stage tower belongs.

publicRoutes.first: PUBLIC ENTRANCE. The glazed pair is chained under the closure order; the service entrance is around the block.
PUBLIC ROOMS: HALL, BATHS, CHAPEL, PRACTICE WING. Several arrows have been amended in three different hands.
publicRoutes.again: The building kept changing after the sign was made.

publicRoutes.first: CONCERT HALL — STALLS / GALLERIES. The gilt house lettering survives above the acoustic pair.
A painted sign over a gap in the east wall: TOWER — RINGING CHAMBER — NO ADMITTANCE TO THE PUBLIC.
publicRoutes.again: Somebody has added BELLS UP underneath it, in a different hand and a different decade.

publicRoutes.first: RINGING ROOM. The enamel letters are older than the electrical conduit.
BELLS — AUTHORISED ACCESS. The final word has been underlined by hand.
ORGAN LOFT / NAVE. An arrow follows the service stair down.
NAVE / CHAPEL EXIT. The route continues through the narthex to the public doors.

chapelInscriptions.first: The hymn board still reads 17 · 44 · 91. Nobody cleared the last service.
J. VALE & SONS — CAST FOR ELLERY COLLEGIATE CHAPEL — 1908. Eight bells. Tenor: 2,200 kg.
chapelInscriptions.again: Ellery Collegiate Chapel. 1908. No county is given.

chapelInscriptions.first: ELLERY COLLEGIATE CHAPEL — STEDMAN TRIPLES — 1908. A touch, not a peal.
chapelInscriptions.again: The gilt names have gone brown.

chapelInscriptions.first: CLOCK HAMMER ISOLATOR. A red lever, mechanically linked.

workplacePaper.first: A dead donation till. The paper roll reads THANK YOU FOR HELPING US KEEP THE BELLS SOUNDING.
workplacePaper.again: No power. The last receipt remains uncut.

workplacePaper.first: One chapel pew never made it upstairs. A paper removal tag is still tied to it.
workplacePaper.again: The tag says RETURN TO CHAPEL.

workplacePaper.first: A tray stencilled RETURNS, with nothing in it. The word came with the tray.
workplacePaper.again: RETURNED is the column the work order will not close without. Different building, same word.

workplacePaper.first: HEADER 3 — ISOLATION. Back nut, then gland, then handwheel, in that order, all three home before the line is dead. Clockwise to close, and the card is emphatic about it.
workplacePaper.again: The last line is in a different hand: the bypass cock feeds the return and is NOT part of this header. Somebody learned that the hard way.

servicePanelCodes.first: The natatorium distribution panel, S/P-02, matches the plant-room and front-of-house boxes. Chlorine has lifted the paint beneath its lower lip; every breaker is open.
servicePanelCodes.again: S/P-02. Same installation, different air, no live circuit.

servicePanelCodes.first: The front-of-house panel, S/P-03. Its typed circuit card lists the Scene Dock, foyer and box office; the main isolator is down.
servicePanelCodes.again: S/P-03. A neat card for three dead circuits.

servicePanelCodes.first: The practice-floor panel, S/P-04. Room numbers have been pencilled over a typed teaching-wing schedule; every breaker is open.
servicePanelCodes.again: S/P-04. The pencil is newer than the dead ballast.

servicePanelCodes.first: The academic-floor panel, S/P-05, is fixed to the loggia wall where the stair arrives. Gallery and classroom banks are listed separately; every breaker is open.
servicePanelCodes.again: S/P-05. Last in the numbered run, nearest the way down.

servicePanelCodes.first: The plant-room distribution panel, S/P-01. It begins the same numbered installation as the later boxes upstairs; two typed labels have been corrected in pencil.
servicePanelCodes.again: S/P-01. The oldest corrections are still the clearest instructions.

explicitExistingStamps.again: FOH/F-01. The replacement cushion still sits higher than the others.

explicitExistingStamps.again: FOH/F-06. It has been sat in since it was put here.

explicitExistingStamps.first: The west console of the foyer suite, FOH/F-04. A long pale tide mark follows the wall side; the inventory stamp is dry beneath it.
explicitExistingStamps.again: FOH/F-04. Water above, old ink below.
